summary.text: Clay Higgins is the U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District, an Army veteran and former law enforcement officer who won the seat in a December 2016 runoff in his first race for public office. He is a core member of the House Freedom Caucus, a senior member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, chairs its Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, and also sits on the House Armed Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born August 24, 1961, in New Orleans; his family moved to Covington, Louisiana, when he was six. He graduated from Covington High School and attended Louisiana State University.
Army veteran; his campaign website says he received his initial police training as a military police officer in the U.S. Army.

Spent much of his career in law enforcement, and maintains an active commission and Louisiana State POST certification. The Advocate described him in 2016 as a reserve deputy for the Lafayette City Marshal's Office and a former captain with the St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office.
The Advocate described him as a viral Crime Stoppers video star and reported that he ran as a tough-talking outsider in his first bid for public office.

Finished second in the November 8, 2016 open-seat primary (26 percent, behind Scott Angelle's 29 percent) and defeated Angelle, a fellow Republican, in the December 10, 2016 runoff by about 12 percentage points; took office January 3, 2017.

Serves as a senior member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and as Chairman of its Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee; also serves on the House Armed Services Committee's Subcommittees on Seapower and Projection Forces and on Readiness.
His official biography describes him as a core member of the House Freedom Caucus and says the Center for Effective Lawmaking ranked him among the most effective Republican legislators in the House.
Resides in Lafayette with his wife, Becca.
